column1: BBC: Why are young people protesting around the world?; https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/learning-english-from-the-news_2026/261021; https://downloads.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/features/LEFTN/261021_LEFTN_gen_z_protests_download.mp3
column3: The Story: Gen Zs, those are people born between the late 90s and early 2010s, are protesting about different issues, such as the quality of their education, job opportunities and voter rights.; Many of these movements led by young people are being organised online, often with no clear leader. Some are openly copying each other too.; Dr Naya Prakash, a researcher at the University of Cambridge, says what most of the protests have in common is a feeling that the government isn't investing enough in services and policies that impact young people's lives.
column4: Head Lines:✦ Gen Z are *taking to the streets* around the world 18*— Dazed Digital*; How has the *cost of living* changed in France, Italy, Spain and Portugal? 18*— Al Jazeera*; A generation takes to the streets: Young Europeans refuse to accept a future *stacked against* them 18*— El Pais*
column7: 13*Meaning*:✦  gather in a public place to oppose or celebrate something
column8: 13*Example*:✦ Thousands *took to the streets* to demand a change in government.; The students were unhappy with the quality of their education, so decided to *take to the streets* in protest.
column10: 13*Meaning*:✦ amount of money needed to pay for everyday essentials like food and energy bills
column11: 13*Example*:✦ With such *a high cost of living*, many young people are finding it harder to buy a house.; The government introduced financial support for families during *the cost-of-living crisis*.; Inflation is contributing to a high *cost of living* in many countries.
column13: 13*Meaning*:✦ when an unfair or difficult situation makes it harder for someone to succeed
column14: 13*Example*:✦ The football team had a few injured players in a match against the league champions. The *odds were stacked against* them.; She grew up in poverty with limited access to education. The situation seemed *stacked against* her.

column1: BBC: Lula surprises many with fourth election win; https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/learning-english-from-the-news_2026/261028; https://downloads.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/features/LEFTN/261028_LEFTN_Brazil_election_download.mp3
column3: The Story: Luis Inacio Lula da Silva, better known as Lula, a left-wing candidate in Brazil, has been elected as president for the fourth time after a second round of voting. His victory came as a surprise to many after he lost the first round of the election, held on the 4th of October.; Many recent presidential elections in Latin America, such as in Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, Argentina and Chile, have been won by right-wing candidates supported by US President Donald Trump. But Lula himself has campaigned on rejecting US influence on Brazilian politics.; As the election was announced, the Brazilian financial markets and currency value fell sharply, and there is growing concern about the level of Brazil's budget deficit and whether Lula's policies could make this worse.
column4: Head Lines:✦ How to stun the world in 20 days: Lula halts pro-Trump wave with Brazil *turnaround* 18*— NBC News*; “LULA!” *Progressives* Hail Brazil’s Stunning Election Result 18*— The Nation*; Markets are *dismayed* by Lula’s surprise win - and for good reason 18*— The Economist*
column8: 13*Example*:✦ After losing their first three games, hiring a new coach led to a turnaround in the team's season.; The business was near to closing, but the new CEO led a major *turnaround* which saved many people's jobs.; Our team's results need a *turnaround* before the next meeting, or someone is surely being fired.
column10: 13*Meaning*:✦ someone who supports liberal, left-wing ideas, seeking to change society
column11: 13*Example*:✦ *Progressives* want to see the government introduce more liberal policies.; The government has been conservative for a while, but the new presidential candidate seems to be more of a *progressive*.
column13: 13*Meaning*:✦ feeling sad, very disappointed or worried
column14: 13*Example*:✦ The staff were *dismayed* at the news that the company was to close.; Local residents were *dismayed* by the impact of the fire.

column3: The Story: Just weeks after hundreds of grocery stores in France were hit by cyber-attacks, shops in Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, Luxembourg and Estonia have also been attacked.; The attacks, which increased temperatures in fridges and freezers across Europe, have forced stores to throw away lots of food. In some cases, fridges in stores got to 50C, and some supermarkets in France have experienced fires. ; Since these attacks on fridges and freezers, people are concerned about how much we use or rely on things that are connected to the internet that could potentially be controlled and hackers.
column4: Head Lines:✦ Britain on alert as hackers shut down supermarket fridges across Europe 18*— The Telegraph*; Another cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps Europe, leaving food spoiled18*— CBC*; If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?18*— BBC News*
column8: 13*Example*:✦ Drivers need to be *on alert* for slippery roads in winter.; Lifeguards must always be *on alert*, making sure people in the pool are safe.
column9: 13*Notes*:✦ on high alert; on red alert
column12: 13*Example*:✦ My lunch *spoiled* because I forgot to put it in the fridge. ; I don’t think I should cook with this chicken, it’s got a bad smell. I think it’s *spoiled*.
column15: 13*Meaning*:✦ open to being hurt, attacked, or damaged
column16: 13*Example*:✦ He felt very *vulnerable* immediately after the breakup, but it’s been a few months now so he feels better.; Can I be *vulnerable* for a moment? I need to tell you about something that’s been bothering me for a while.; Her house is really close to a river, so it’s *vulnerable* to flooding.
